voyage.name: Palermo Cathedral
voyage.content: Honey-coloured and Catalan influenced. Frederick II, Barbarossa's grandson, died in 1250 and is buried here, far from his ancestral home above Hohenstaufen, Germany. Frederick's sarcophagus is of porphyry dyed with imperial purple.

voyage.name: Palatine Chapel
voyage.price: included in the Normans palace tickets
voyage.content: It's one of the artistic gems of Palermo: a chapel with magnificent mosaics and Arabian-style decorations, among the most beautiful in the world. It is inside of Palazzo dei Normanni.

voyage.name: Palazzo dei Normanni
voyage.content: The oldest royal residence in Europe, the home of the rulers of the Kingdom of Sicily and imperial seat of the Emperor Frederick II. The palace contains the Cappella Palatina, the best example of the Arab-Norman style of Sicily. Nowadays it is the seat of the Sicilian Parliament.

voyage.name: San Giovanni degli Eremiti
voyage.content: Church notable for its brilliant red domes, which show the persistence of the Arab influences in the 12th century, with its typical Arab-Norman style. The €6 admission ensures that the lovely garden is quiet and peaceful.

voyage.name: Catacombe dei Cappuccini
voyage.content: The catacombs of the Capuchin convent contain over 8,000 mummified ex-residents from Palermo and its surrounding villages, some merely clothed skeletons, other remarkably well-preserved and lifelike. Well worth a visit, interesting, if slightly morbid. Children may either find it exciting or terrifying, and it must be the responsibility of their parents to think carefully before taking them. You can arrive via the tr

voyage.name: Church of the Gesù
voyage.content: The Gesu Church is one of the most architecturally important in Palermo. Constructed between 1564–1633, its late date of completion resulted in an abundant use of polychrome marbles on both floors and walls. This form of decoration, which gradually evolved in Sicily from the beginning of the 17th century, was a mark of the beginning of the Sicilian Baroque period, which was to give Sicily almost an architectural nati

voyage.name: Piazza Pretoria and the Fontana Pretoria
voyage.alt: also known as square of Shame
voyage.content: In 1573 the Senate of Palermo bought a fountain intended for the Palace of San Clemente in Florence, with the intention of placing it in the square. The large central fountain is the focal point for 16 nude statues of nymphs, humans, mermaids and satyrs. In 1860, the fountain was considered the representation of corrupt municipalities, and Palermo nicknamed the square with the nudity of the statues, the Square of Sha

voyage.name: Praetorian Palace or Palace of the Eagles
voyage.alt: Palazzo Pretorio or Palazzo delle Aquile
voyage.content: The building has an important role in the political life of the city, since it houses the mayor and the offices of the municipality of Palermo. Construction began in 1463. It is open for visits to see the sumptuous meeting rooms, the "Sala Rossa" (seat of the mayor), the "Sala Gialla" (seat of the municipal government), the "Sala delle Lapidi" (seat of the city council), and the "Sala Garibaldi".

voyage.name: Monreale
voyage.content: A village 8 km west of Palermo, sitting on the hill with a great view back towards the city and the sea. It is home to a historical Norman-Byzantine cathedral, which has been designated as one of several buildings named in a UNESCO World Heritage Site

voyage.name: Monreale Cathedral
voyage.content: The cathedral of Monreale is one of the greatest extant examples of Norman architecture. It was begun in 1174 by William II and completed four years later. The church is a national monument of Italy and one of the most important attractions of Sicily. The cloister has 228 small columns, each with different decorations influenced by Provençal, Burgundian, Arab and Salerno medieval art.

voyage.name: Palermo Botanical Garden
voyage.hours: Opens at 09:00, closes at different times based on the season (e.g. 17:00 in winter, 20:00 in summer)
voyage.content: Historical city botanical gardens featuring many collections of plants, trees, and aquaculture. The garden is associated with the neighbouring university and contains a number of experimental gardens to test acclimation of plant species to Sicily.

voyage.name: Museo delle Maioliche (Museum of Maiolica Tile)
voyage.content: Beautiful private museum of historical tiles produced both locally and in Naples. Guided tours available in English or Italian will take you through the techniques and historical considerations of tile making and its importance across Italy.

voyage.name: Isola Saporita
voyage.content: Corso Vittorio Emanuele 504 (opposite the cathedral). Good selection of wine, oil, marmalade, sauces, etc.

voyage.name: Mercato di Ballarò
voyage.content: Busy food market in Albergheria.

voyage.name: La Coppola Storta
voyage.content: This cap, first worn by Sicilian peasants and later by the Mafia, has become a stylish accessory.

voyage.name: Stuzzicandoci
voyage.content: Best place to eat a delicious arancina in Palermo downtown. The owner is really kind and friendly. Quality ingredients and courteous staff.

voyage.name: Timilia
voyage.content: Very good pizzeria, a real delight. Also Vegan options. For those intolerant to gluten and lactose, the pizzas are gluten-free and the mozzarella is lactose-free.

voyage.name: Maqueda Bistrot
voyage.content: Great place, very delicious pasta and the bruschetta with the mozarella is tasty. They serve both pasta and great burgers.

voyage.name: Vecchia Trattoria da Totò
voyage.content: The real Palermo cuisine. Informal trattoria with tables also outdoors. Good mixed fried food, excellent mussels. No English menu.

voyage.name: Bisso Bistrot
voyage.content: Bistro in the centre of Palermo with a wide choice of vegetarian and vegan dishes. Beautiful restaurant, with retro air, very unique old bookstore. Smiling waitress, very good food, decent waiting time.

voyage.name: Il Proverbio
voyage.content: Discesa dei Giudici, 24. Close to station and Quattro Canti. Great Sicilian food, most dishes are €4-6.

voyage.name: Bangla Fast Food
voyage.content: Delicious Indian/Bangladeshi food. Great veg curry, daal and rice for €4. A good selection of samosas and pakoras. Excellent chai for €1.

voyage.name: 100 Montaditos
voyage.content: Many types of sandwiches, all very good. You have to fill in the order sheet and go to the cashier to pay, then the dishes ordered on the sheet arrive. Each sandwich is €1.

voyage.name: Cala Pollo & Co.
voyage.content: In this deli you will find one of the best chicken that the city can offer. Yummy food. Best Italian style BBQ chicken.

voyage.name: Pani câ Meusa – Porta Carbone
voyage.content: The best sandwiches. Excellent typical Palermo food. A dining experience to try these local Street food delicacies.

voyage.name: Le Tabarin
voyage.content: Magical Palermo atmosphere with a background of 1990s/2000s music. One of the best apericena: tasty limoncello Spritz, tasty fresh food, big amount per person.

voyage.name: Voglia Di Pizza
voyage.content: Very tasty and juicy pizza, the dough is just amazing. Inexpensive, plentiful and well stocked with quality ingredients, fast servers.

voyage.name: Osteria dei Vespri
voyage.content: This location has a certain charm, with a quite rare calm in Palermo. The service is impeccable. The vegetarian menu was really good. Delicious wines and fantastic food!

voyage.name: Il Cambusone
voyage.content: Great fish and very kind, attentive staff. Cozy environment, excellent for tasting the flavors of Sicily.

voyage.name: The Bar Brothers
voyage.content: Great little bar for beers and cocktails. A small number of seats out on the street. Beers from €2.50 to 3.50.

voyage.name: dal Barone
voyage.content: Nice wine bar with a good selection of wines. Good cheeseboards.

voyage.name: B&B Novecento
voyage.content: Original liberty style building in the historical centre, three-star B&B with rooms with AC, WiFi, private bathroom (external or also ensuite), central heating, LCD tv, mini bar, frigo, original furnishings of early 1900s.

voyage.name: Villa Addaura
voyage.content: Villa Addaura, a bed and breakfast in Mondello, is in a beautiful location 10 metres from the sea.

voyage.name: B&B Teatro Massimo
voyage.content: Bed and breakfast Teatro Massimo is an elegant residence in the heart of Palermo, 50 m from the Teatro Massimo, in the pedestrian area of the historical centre. The historic building is completely restored and has an elevator. The B&B offers accommodation in rooms and elegantly furnished apartments. They are air-conditioned, equipped with TV and WiFi.

voyage.name: B&B Palermo A Casa di Amici
voyage.content: In the historic centre of Palermo near Al Teatro Massimo.

voyage.name: Al Giardino Dell'Alloro
voyage.content: On a quiet street.

voyage.name: Hotel Casa Giuditta
voyage.content: Offers rooms and self-catering apartments with 17th-century style decorations. Fully furnished with all mod cons: a/c, washing machines, kitchen with oven, freezer, dishwasher, satellite TV. Children welcome.

voyage.name: Palermo Sea Holidays
voyage.content: A group of 1- and 2-bedroom self-catering apartments, on Sferracavallo's seafront close to Palermo. Simple but comfortable studios have an outdoor yard, for relaxing during the day and romantic dinners by night. Sferracavallo has good public transport connections to Palermo, and is close to the Capo Gallo nature reserve.

voyage.name: Florio Park Hotel
voyage.content: First category hotel complex by the sea on a beautiful golden and sandy beach. Inside a 4-hectare park, the hotel has 17 pavilions (1 or 2 floors), surrounded by luxuriant vegetation, that comprise 204 rooms and 6 suites. In the central building you'll find the reception desk and the wide and elegant hall, the restaurant, the excursions office, the American bar, the bazaar and the TV room.

voyage.name: Saint Thorn Guest Club
voyage.address: Via Spina Santa 210, Capo Gallo, near Mondello
voyage.content: It's inside the 'Capo Gallo' nature reserve in the hills outside Palermo, offering stunning views across Mondello's beach. Free parking in the nearby private street, or inside the villa for €5; swimming pool; free internet. All rooms have en suite baths, TV, hair dryer, a/c, fridge, own outside access. Two rooms have kitchenette, with minimum stay of 5 days. Downtown Palermo is about 15 min by bus/car, Mondello 10 mi

voyage.name: Hotel Artemisia Palace Palermo
voyage.content: Elegant four-star hotel which has 18 double rooms and suite. All with private bar, satellite TV with Sky channels, internet connection. Also available a free public parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Italy
voyage.content: Good clean rooms with new bathrooms, AC, TV, and balcony with clotheslines. €60, no breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Joli
voyage.content: Rooms adorned with frescoes and fine decor. Fine service, too.

voyage.name: NH Palermo
voyage.content: Spacious rooms and a congress centre with 2 meeting rooms, all equipped with natural light, on the picturesque gulf of the city and enjoys breathtaking views across the sea.

voyage.name: B&B Porta di Castro
voyage.content: It is an old building restored and well furnished.

voyage.name: B&B Lincoln Suite Palermo
voyage.content: Refined, cheap and central, close to the station.

voyage.name: In Itinera B&B
voyage.alt: near the Giardino Inglese and the Notarbartolo Station
voyage.content: Bed and breakfast art and design in the heart of Palermo. Rooms with free wifi, minibar, bathroom with shower or bath and Chromotherapy, air conditioning

voyage.name: Excelsior Palace Hotel
voyage.content: One of the oldest and most renowned luxury hotels in Palermo. 4 star, near the harbour and the English Garden.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel et Des Palmes Palermo
voyage.content: Large and luxurious 4-star in the centre, with exquisite interior design and high quality service. Also one of the oldest and best known in the city. Richard Wagner stayed here from November 1881 until 20 March 1882. It was at this hotel that he completed Parsifal on 13 January 1882.

voyage.name: Hotel Residenza D’Aragona
voyage.content: Elegant and filled with modern comforts and impeccable service. In the historical centre, near the Politeama and Massimo theaters.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa Igiea Palermo
voyage.content: 5-star villa and hotel complex in the hills overlooking Palermo and the bay. Offering health spa, tennis courts and a fantastic Greek swimming pool that overlooks the sea from on high.

voyage.name: Mondello Palace Hotel
voyage.content: It rises a few meters from the soft and golden sandy beach and is surrounded by a lush Mediterranean park. It is an elegant building with wide, classic halls. There are an open-air swimming pool, free WiFi internet connection and a parking lot inside the hotel (unguarded). The restaurant is the feather in its cap. It is located in a wide and bright hall, opening up on the garden. Here you can taste Sicilian and inter

voyage.name: NH Collection Palermo Palazzo Sitano
voyage.content: Stylish 4‑star hotel centrally located on Via Vittorio Emanuele, steps from Palermo Cathedral and Teatro Massimo. Housed in a beautifully restored Baroque palace, with modern amenities including spa, rooftop terrace, fitness centre, and fine buffet breakfast. Excellent staff, clean rooms, and a popular option for both business and leisure travellers. Some street‑facing rooms may be noisy at weekends.
